name: Rolling mean
brief:
A rolling mean averages the last few values and moves along one step at a time. Traders use it to smooth a price series and to build trend signals. pandas does it with `.rolling(window).mean()`; here you build it by hand so you know what that line computes.

Write `rolling_mean(values, window)`. It returns the mean of every run of `window` consecutive values, in order.
definition:
With values $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ and window $w$, the mean ending at position $i$ is

$$m_i = \dfrac{1}{w} \sum_{j=i-w+1}^{i} x_j, \quad i = w - 1, \dots, n - 1$$

That gives $n - w + 1$ means. Return an empty list when $w > n$. The window is always at least 1.
constraints: $O(n)$ time. Recomputing each window from scratch is $O(nw)$ and runs out of time on the long test.
Standard library only. NumPy and pandas are not loaded.
All tests share a 5-second time limit.
hint: Keep a running sum of the current window. When the window moves one step, add the new value and subtract the one that just left.

tests.name: Window of one
tests.why: A window of 1 holds one value, so each mean is the value itself.

tests.name: Window as long as the list
tests.why: There is exactly one full window, so return a list with one mean.

tests.name: Window too long
tests.why: There is no full window of 3 in two values. Return an empty list.

tests.name: Empty list
tests.why: No values means no windows. Return an empty list.

tests.name: Negative values
tests.why: Each window holds the last `window` values only. Drop the oldest as the newest comes in.

tests.name: Not a cumulative mean
tests.why: Average the last 3 values, not every value so far. The window moves along.

tests.name: Daily closes
tests.why: Return one mean per full window, in order, as floats.

tests.name: Long series, sampled
tests.note: 100,000 prices, window 1,000; five means are checked
tests.why: This test has 100,000 values and a window of 1,000. Summing every window afresh takes about $10^8$ steps; a running sum takes $10^5$.

tests.name: Long series, length
tests.why: There are $n - w + 1 = 99{,}001$ full windows. A window starts at every position that leaves room for 1,000 values.

how: Submit runs 9 hidden tests, two of them on 100,000 values with a window of 1,000. Lists are compared element by element, and each float counts when it is within a relative 1e-9 of the expected value.
where: Prepares 1.1 level 3, time series in pandas: the same computation `.rolling()` performs.
notes: The first window is summed once. After that each step costs one addition and one subtraction.
`values[i - window]` is the value that just left the window.
This is what pandas computes for `.rolling(window).mean()`, without the leading `NaN` values.

def _walk(n, seed, start, step):
    # Seeded random walk from an integer LCG, so every Python makes the same prices
    x = seed
    p = start
    out = []
    for _ in range(n):
        x = (x * 1103515245 + 12345) % 2147483648
        p = p * (1 + step * ((x % 2001 - 1000) / 1000))
        out.append(p)
    return out
